newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds up in thin mkt as local banks buy.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds up in thin mkt as local banks buy.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Monday, as a trickle of domestic bank buying kept the market afloat amid thin pre-Christmas trade.
"The market was firm, but there was very little trade," said a trader at an Argentine brokerage house.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.30 to 122.85, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/8 to 86-6/8.
The market was led by Argentina's Brady bonds which followed the lead set by firmer U.S. Treasuries.
"Latin Brady bonds used a steady to firm Treasury bond bias to extend last week's rally in light pre-holiday trade," said MMS International in an investor note.

Traders said they did not expect much activity through the rest of the week because of Christmas. The market is only officially shut on Wednesday although many players will be away for the rest of the week meaning trade is set to be slim.
Otherwise, traders said local banks may take the opportunity of the light trade during these two weeks to quietly build up their holdings of bonds for the coming year.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.65 percent from 6.85 percent.
